data.title: Gold price falls as Fed hike odds jump and GLD, IAU ETF outflows surge
data.description:
Gold price remained under pressure on Thursday as investors bet that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next meeting. The metal traded at $3,728, about $32 above this week’s low of $3,696. It remains well below its all-time high of $5,600, and technical indicators suggest further downside in the near term.

Gold price has slumped amid Fed rate hike odds

Gold has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months as demand among investors waned. ETF Database data shows that the SPDR Gold ETF (GLD) has had over $1.37 billion in outflows in the last 30 days. The iShares Gold Trust (IAU) has shed over $279 million in assets in the same period. 

Investors are concerned about the rising probability that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates in the coming meeting. The bank has already hiked rates by 25 basis points, and there is a consensus that it will hike in the coming meeting. Odds of the hike happening have jumped to over 99% on Polymarket. 

Minutes released on Wednesday showed that Federal Reserve officials struck a hawkish tone at their last meeting, even though they held interest rates steady. Rather than raise rates, they chose to pause while they gather more information on inflation and the economy.

Recent numbers have confirmed their view that inflation is still stubbornly high. The most recent data showed that the headline and core Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% and 0.3%, respectively. Inflation has remained above the 2% target in the last five years, and this trend may continue as President Donald Trump considers launching fresh attacks against Iran.

Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data showed that the labor market remained strong last month. The most recent data showed that the American economy created over 165k jobs as the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%. Retail sales remained resilient last month.

Gold has also dropped amid elevated bond yields. The ten-year yield crossed the important resistance level of 5% and has remained above it in the past few weeks. Short-term yields have also continued rising, making gold less attractive. 

Central banks are buying gold

On the positive side, central banks have continued to accumulate gold this year. The most active ones are from China, Uzbekistan, and Poland. In total, central banks have bought 170 tons of gold, which are currently worth about $21 billion. The real figure is much higher than that since many countries don’t provide the most accurate data.

Gold may also benefit from the rising US debt, which has jumped to over $40.6 trillion, a few months after it crossed the crucial $40 trillion milestone. The metal is widely seen as a good hedge against the rising spending by US authorities.

Gold price technical analysis

Gold chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that gold has been in a strong downward trend in the past few months. Most recently, it dropped from a high of $4,695 in August to the current $3,737.

Gold has slumped below the important support level of $3,946, its lowest level on June 30th. It has remained below the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has continued falling.

Therefore, gold will likely continue falling in the near term, with the next psychological level to watch will be at $3,500. On the flip side, a move above the resistance level of $3,946 will invalidate the bearish outlook and point to more gains. The next key catalysts for gold will be the nonfarm payrolls, inflation, and the December Federal Reserve interest rate decision.

data.title: Samsung and SK Hynix stocks fall again as Nvidia earnings boost fades
data.description:
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix stocks fell on Thursday, reversing part of their previous session's gains as Nvidia's record earnings failed to restore lasting confidence in the artificial intelligence trade.

Samsung declined 2.4% and SK Hynix lost 1.3% by 11:20 am in Seoul. The benchmark KOSPI slipped 0.94% to 5,019.72, having briefly traded below 5,000.

The weakness followed a 2.89% decline in Nvidia's US shares on Wednesday, despite the chipmaker reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly sales and an upbeat forecast.

Nvidia earnings impact: Rally quickly loses momentum

Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion on Tuesday, an increase of 103% from a year earlier. Its data-centre division generated $107.6 billion, while management projected about $130 billion in sales for the following quarter.

The figures reinforced expectations of sustained spending on AI infrastructure and initially lifted South Korean semiconductor shares.

On Wednesday, Samsung rose 2.31% to 194,700 won and SK Hynix gained 4.19% to 1,144,000 won. The KOSPI advanced 1.99%, recovering from its previous close below 5,000.

But Nvidia's decline during the subsequent US session suggested investors were reluctant to treat one strong earnings report as proof that AI investments will deliver attractive returns.

Neil Shah, vice-president of research at Counterpoint, told Reuters the results had stabilised sentiment but “postponed rather than permanently cured investor anxiety”.

Concerns over data-centre financing, export restrictions and Nvidia's management transition following Jensen Huang's resignation continue to cloud the outlook.

Foreign selling adds pressure to South Korea semiconductor stocks

Investors outside South Korea were net sellers of 216.55 billion won in KOSPI shares by 11:20 am Thursday. Institutions sold another 159.27 billion won, while retail investors bought 278.79 billion won.

The outflows help explain why shares have struggled to hold gains despite impressive semiconductor earnings and resilient demand for memory chips.

Samsung and SK Hynix have benefited from elevated prices for high-bandwidth memory and server DRAM.

But buyers of their shares are increasingly looking beyond current orders to ask how long those margins can endure.

More production capacity, delayed data-centre construction or weaker cloud spending could eventually bring tighter competition and lower pricing power.

Jung Hee-chan of Samsung Futures told Money Today that technology companies should lead Korean earnings growth next year, although investors need greater confidence that profits can be sustained before rewarding the sector with higher valuations.

Samsung, SK Hynix stocks: Is semiconductor sell-off becoming excessive?

US monetary policy is adding another challenge. Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting, released Wednesday, showed that almost all officials expected further interest-rate increases would be appropriate under their baseline outlooks.

Higher yields can make future earnings less valuable in today's terms, weighing heavily on technology companies priced for years of growth.

Thursday's planned Nasdaq debut of AI developer Anthropic is another test of investor appetite for expensive technology businesses.

Still, not every analyst sees the downturn as justified.

Kiwoom Securities analyst Han Ji-young told Seoul Economic Daily that South Korean share prices already reflect much of the foreseeable economic and AI-related uncertainty.

A less negative market response and improving foreign flows could therefore support a rebound.

data.title: Lenovo Group stock analysis after earnings: is this Dell rival a buy or sell?
data.description:
Lenovo Group stock remained under pressure on Thursday after the technology company published its financial results. It was trading at H$16.72, down by over 55% from its all-time high. Its technicals suggest that it has more downside in the near term. 

Lenovo Group’s business continued doing well

Lenovo Group, a leading competitor to Dell and HP Enterprise, reported strong financial results for the latest quarter. The figures show the company’s business continued to grow, driven by ongoing investment in artificial intelligence (AI).

The results showed that its revenue growth gained momentum. Its revenue soared by 46% YoY to $30.2 billion, with its AI related figure rising by 79. 

A look at its segments shows the business is thriving. The Intelligent Devices Group generated more than $17.4 billion in revenue, up 17% year on year, with an operating margin of 7.1%. This growth came as the company prioritized higher-priced devices, even as the number of units sold fell. 

Indeed, its premium PCs contributed to 63% of all PC shippings during the quarter. Recent data by Gartner showed that its PC sales dropped by 22.4% to 14.9 million during the quarter. Its PC margins have also dropped because of the ongoing memory shortage.

The Infrastructure Solutions Group’s revenue surged 178%, and its AI server pipeline reached $54 billion. 

Lenovo’s AI business is being driven by American hyperscalers, neoclouds, and Asian data center companies. Some of the revenue is coming from Asian data centers, especially in places like China and Malaysia. Lenovo’s Solutions and Services Group (SSG) grew by 205 to $3.1 billion. 

Still, the company made a $713 million loss during the quarter after losing over $1.19 billion in the same period last year. The loss was driven by fair value loss of $3.9 billion on derivative financial liabilities. 

Concerns about AI growth remains

Lenovo Group and other competitors have dropped in the past few months. For example, Dell stock has plunged by 46% from its highest point this year. It has dropped to its lowest level since May 28 this year.

HP Enterprise has also dropped to $45.78, down by 37% from the year-to-date high, while Super Micro Computer (SMCI) dropped by 52% in this period. Other companies in the AI space like Micron, SanDisk, and Western Digital have all plunged.

Investors are concerned about the potential slowdown in the coming months that would impact demand for its products. 

On the positive side, there are signs that demand is continuing growing. For example, Nvidia’s earnings report showed that its revenue jumped to $115 billion in the third quarter, much higher than the expected $108 billion. 

Lenovo Group stock technical analysis

Lenovo Group stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Lenovo Group’s stock has continued its strong sell-off in the past few months. It has slumped from $37 in September to the current $16.7. This retreat coincided with the ongoing weakness of other top companies in the AI space.

The stock has dropped below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level of $19.73. In most cases, moving below that retracement normally confirms a bearish breakout. 

The stock has dropped below the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA) and the two lines are about to cross each other. A crossover would lead to a death cross, a popular bearish outlook.

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the key support level of $14.78, the 78.6% retracement level. A move below that level will point to more losses towards $10. In the future, however, there is a likelihood that the stock will bounce back, potentially to $20 and above.

data.title: Soybean price analysis: Brent oil price bounces off crucial support
data.description:
Soybean price is trading within a rather tight range as investors weigh the energy market and the overall supply/demand dynamics. The bulls attempts of a breakout late last week were unsuccessful as the differing factors failed to attract enough buyers. In the short term, sideways trading may continue, with a breakout being dependent on crucial resistance levels. 

Soybean price trades sideways amid a volatile energy market

CBOT soybean price has been trading sideways in recent sessions after easing from the bullish WASDE report. USDA’s forecast for the 2026/27 season included increased exports and lower ending stocks. This is despite the predicted surge in US production by 12 million bushels. US soybean exports are expected to increase by 25 million bushels while the global ending stocks have been lessened by 0.8 million tons. 

According to the latest NASS crop progress report, soybean harvesting is 96% complete across the United States. This is slightly higher than the average pace of 95%. 

At the same time, the Export Inspections data indicate that soybean shipments for the week that ended on 12th November were 1.708 million metric tonnes (MMT). This was a decline of 10.8% from the previous week, but an increase of 41.7% from a similar period in 2025. Notably, China was the leading destination with a shipment of 691,670 MT. Increased US exports and brisk Chinese demand continue to support soybean prices. 

However, a stronger US dollar and weaker Brazilian Real are curbing the asset’s price gains. Earlier on Tuesday, the  Brazilian Real extended its losses to a fresh 19-month low before easing slightly. Over the past three weeks, the South American currency has plunged by close to 15%, enticing local producers to increase export volumes for more US dollars. At the same time, a stronger greenback renders the dollar-priced asset more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies. 

In the ensuing sessions, investors within the soybean market will also be eyeing crude oil prices. The crude oil market has been rather volatile in recent sessions amid conflicting drivers. On the one hand, the persistent conflicts in the Middle East are offering steady support to energy prices. However, investors are increasingly betting on a global supply glut. Crude oil prices largely impact the demand for biofuel. In addition to corn and sugarcane, soybean is a major source of biofuel.  

Soybean price technical analysis

CBOT soybean futures made subtle movements on Tuessday as the agricultural commodity continues to trade sideways. Late last week, the bulls attempted a breakout, surging to a one-and-a-half week high at $12.41 a bushel before easing back to its tight trading range. At the time of writing, soybean price was at $12.29, up by 0.04%.  

A look at its daily chart points to continued sideways trading in the short term, as investors eye the driving fundamentals and technical indicators. To begin with, CBOT soybean price remains below the short-term 25-day EMA and the medium-term 50-day EMA. Indeed, in late October, the two technical indicators formed a bearish death-cross pattern that is still in place. The bearish formation occurs when short-term MA crosses the medium/long-term MA to the downside as an indication of further losses. Besides, its RSI of 46 supports the thesis on curbed gains and range-bound trading. 

Even with these bearish technical indicators, soybean price continues to trade above the long-term 200-day EMA. This is an indication that the long-term support is still intact.  

In line with these technical indicators, and the fundamentals, the range between the support level of $12.14 and the resistance along the 25-day EMA at $12.35 is worth watching. Further gains will likely be curbed at $12.41. On the flip side, additional losses will invalidate this cautious thesis as the sellers eye the lower support level at $12.09.

data.title: Bitcoin price today: BTC below $64,000 as Citi cuts target to $99,532
data.description:
Bitcoin price today slipped further below $64,000 on Wednesday, November 18, after Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin target to $99,532 and as US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung back to outflows ahead of the Federal Reserve's October minutes.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $63,465 on Coinbase at 15:08 UK time, down 2.2% from Tuesday's close of $64,873 at midnight UTC.

Citi cuts its 12-month Bitcoin and Ethereum targets

Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin price target to $99,532 from $113,000 and its Ethereum target to $2,838 from $3,028, according to a research note reported by CNBC on Wednesday.

Citi analyst Alex Saunders said a rangebound crypto market had broken lower and that both assets had fallen since the bank's previous update.

He downgraded Citi's near-term outlook for capital inflows to neutral after Bitcoin dropped below its 200-day moving average.

Saunders pointed to weaker ETF demand, with Bitcoin fund flows in net outflow so far this year and Ethereum funds recording outflows in each of the past seven weeks.

Futures positioning pointed to broader deleveraging, he said, while a stronger US dollar, higher real yields and a rise in equity-market volatility had tightened the backdrop for crypto.

Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 is again running above its correlation with gold, according to the note.

Citi had raised those targets to $113,000 and $3,028 in early October.

Even after the cut, the new Bitcoin target implies about 57% upside from Wednesday's Coinbase price. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, leaving about 60% implied upside to Citi's $2,838 Ethereum target.

What happened to Bitcoin price today?

Bitcoin traded between $63,001 and $64,933 on Coinbase on Wednesday, with sellers capping every move towards $65,000.

The world's largest cryptocurrency is about 16% below its November 9 high of $75,500 on Coinbase.

It hit $61,946 on Coinbase on November 15, its lowest point of the month so far.

The rest of the market was also lower. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, while XRP was at $0.98.

Why is Bitcoin price falling?

ETF demand has faded again, the same pressure Citi cited in its target cut.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $239.9 million on Tuesday, November 17, according to Farside Investors.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $209.5 million of that.

That reversed a small $7.9 million inflow on Monday.

Since October 30, the funds have lost about $3.2 billion in 13 sessions, based on Farside's daily data.

US spot Ether ETFs lost $29.1 million on Tuesday, Farside data show.

Interest rates are the other weight.

The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, but Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike.

On Tuesday, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy "will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027", in remarks in Argentina.

Higher rates make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive.

The US dollar index touched a 52-week high of 103.91 on Wednesday, according to TradingView.

What happens next?

The Fed's minutes from its October 27-28 meeting are due at 19:00 UK time on Wednesday.

Traders will look at how many officials backed a hike and how soon. The Fed's next decision is on December 9.

Bitfinex analysts said in their Bitfinex Alpha report on Monday that they expect Bitcoin to trade between $61,800 and $69,400 this week, with another test of the November 15 low possible.

They named $57,803, Bitcoin's July cycle low, as a key level to watch, and said a recovery above $72,700 with renewed ETF inflows would show selling pressure is fading.

Farside's figures for Wednesday's ETF flows will show whether institutional selling has eased.

Should you buy Bitcoin now?

Bitcoin has held above last week's low, but ETF outflows and a hawkish Fed are still weighing on it.

Citi's reduced 12-month target of $99,532 still sits well above the current price, though that is a forecast, not a recommendation.

A hawkish set of minutes could push Bitcoin back towards $62,000, while a softer tone could bring buyers back.

For more coverage, see our latest cryptocurrency news.

data.title: Anthropic IPO prices at $83 a share as ANT prepares Thursday debut
data.description:
Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, according to CNBC and Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, $5 above the top of the $70–$78 range in the company's latest SEC filing.

Class A shares in the Claude developer are due to begin trading on Thursday, 19 November, on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT.

The $83 price has not yet been locked in a prospectus supplement.

As of late evening in London on 18 November, no Form 424B4 had appeared on EDGAR, and Anthropic had not published a pricing announcement on its newsroom or IPO site.

Until a filing appears, these figures should be read as reported terms, not as a confirmed prospectus price.

Bloomberg also said the size of the offering has increased, without disclosing a new share count.

The marketed deal, in Amendment No. 3 to Anthropic's Form S-1, filed on 17 November, was 825 million Class A shares — 801,351,354 sold by the company and 23,648,646 by existing holders.

On that marketed count, $83 a share would raise $68.475 billion before underwriting discounts, an Invezz calculation.

Actual gross proceeds would be higher if the deal was upsized, as Bloomberg reported. Anthropic would not receive the proceeds from the secondary shares. A separate $26 billion private placement of non-voting Class N shares is due to close at the IPO price.

How does $83 compare with the filed range?

The official range was never raised in a filing. Amendment No. 3 still estimated $70.00 to $78.00 a share. At $78, the 825 million shares would have raised $64.35 billion gross, as set out in our note on Anthropic's $70–$78 IPO price range.

Earlier on Wednesday, CNBC reported that Anthropic was considering selling more than 825 million shares and was weighing a price well above $80.

The Wall Street Journal had reported on 17 November that Anthropic expected to price above $80, and said that would value the company at about $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion.

The prospectus granted the underwriters, represented by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a 30-day option to buy up to 123.75 million additional Class A shares. Whether that greenshoe was resized with any upsizing of the base deal has not been disclosed.

What valuation does $83 imply?

The filing does not state a single official valuation, and the final figure will depend on the share count used, including any upsizing.

Coverage of the prospectus has put the fully diluted value at about $1.405 trillion at the $78 top of the range. A like-for-like move to $83 would imply about $1.50 trillion. That is an illustration, not a number in a pricing prospectus, and it would change if more shares have been added.

How strong was demand?

CNBC reported on Wednesday morning that institutional demand was around $400 billion and that retail demand was approaching $100 billion. Those figures were described as indications of interest, not binding orders.

What happens next?

Trading is scheduled to start on Thursday under the ANT ticker. Nasdaq, in Data Technical News #2026-28, said Anthropic's Class A common stock is expected to begin trading on 19 November.

Hargreaves Lansdown has told UK applicants that trading is expected from 2:30pm London time (9:30am ET). Investors who received an allocation pay the IPO price; anyone buying once the shares are listed pays the market price. A Form 424B4, when it appears, would be the official confirmation of the price, the final share count and any change to the greenshoe.

If ANT starts trading on 19 November, MSCI has said it would decide on early inclusion no later than before the open of the third trading day, which would be Monday, 23 November. If the stock qualifies, addition would be effective as of the close on 30 November, or 1 December.

FTSE Russell has deferred fast entry because of Thanksgiving: Russell US addition, if confirmed, would be effective 14 December, and FTSE GEIS on 21 December. Nasdaq has not issued a notice adding ANT to the Nasdaq-100. The S&P 500 is not in prospect at listing.

📘 If you are looking to trade the shares on day one, our guide on how to buy Anthropic stock walks through the steps for buying US-listed shares.

📅 We are tracking the price, valuation and timetable on our Anthropic IPO date, valuation and ticker hub.

Thursday's first trade will test whether that demand holds up in public.

data.title: Why is Nvidia stock falling over 2% on Wednesday?
data.description:
Nvidia shares NVDA fell 2.2% on Wednesday, extending their decline to a fifth consecutive session, as the US House Committee on Energy and Commerce demanded a formal briefing from the chipmaker over alleged export control violations and former CEO Jensen Huang's reported links to a suspected Chinese spy.

Representative Brett Guthrie, chairman of the committee, sent a letter to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress requesting that company officials appear before lawmakers no later than December 2.

The inquiry focuses on whether Nvidia circumvented federal restrictions intended to prevent advanced artificial intelligence technology from reaching China.

Lawmakers are also examining allegations that a senior company official attempted to interfere with a federal investigation.

The developments add to the pressure on Nvidia as it navigates a leadership transition and scrutiny over national security concerns, despite strong quarterly results and an upbeat revenue outlook.

Congressional probe focuses on export control allegations

In his letter, Guthrie said the reported events raised questions about Nvidia's compliance with federal export laws and the effectiveness of its security controls.

The congressional investigation centres on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer suspected of helping Chinese companies circumvent US export restrictions.

On November 16, the Justice Department and Commerce Department publicly confirmed a joint criminal investigation into the company.

Reports have also linked Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is alleged to have a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, to suspected Chinese intelligence activities.

According to Guthrie's letter, investigators are examining claims that she established a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia hardware.

Lawmakers are also looking into allegations that the Commerce Department transferred its initial investigation into Megaspeed to the Justice Department last year after Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce officials seeking information about the inquiry.

These allegations have not been established as findings of wrongdoing by Nvidia.

Leadership transition adds to investor concerns

The controversy has coincided with significant changes at Nvidia's senior leadership level.

On November 8, Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair in an internal email to employees and said the company's board had launched an independent investigation into national security concerns raised by media reports.

Four days later, he announced his departure from company leadership.

Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, took over as interim CEO while the company works with an external firm to find a permanent replacement.

The uncertainty has weighed on investor sentiment, with Nvidia shares declining for five consecutive trading sessions and facing the prospect of a seventh consecutive weekly loss.

However, Wall Street analysts have pointed to the company's latest financial results as evidence that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong.

Nvidia reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share, beating analyst expectations by 21 cents.

Revenue reached $115.84 billion, up 103.2% from a year earlier and $7.13 billion above forecasts.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, compared with analyst estimates of $124.89 billion.

The forecast assumes no data centre computing revenue from China.

Analysts remain positive on Nvidia's outlook

Several Wall Street firms have maintained positive views on Nvidia despite the leadership uncertainty.

RBC reiterated its Outperform rating, citing demand that continues to exceed supply, a product roadmap extending over the next three years and limited near-term competitive risks due to industry supply constraints.

The firm also highlighted rising supply purchase commitments as evidence of strong demand visibility.

Morgan Stanley maintained its Overweight rating, pointing to strong demand for AI computing and Nvidia's competitive position.

Its analysts also viewed the company's willingness to provide forward-looking commentary as a positive.

Wedbush raised its price target to $293 from $275 while retaining an Outperform rating.

The firm said Nvidia's near- and medium-term demand outlook remained unchanged despite Huang's departure.

The company also has $227.3 billion remaining under its share buyback authorisation.

Kress described returning capital to shareholders as a top priority during the earnings call and said Nvidia could fully utilise the remaining authorisation by fiscal 2028.

Jefferies said the buyback programme offered another potential source of support for the stock, while noting that investors still need greater visibility into the company's strategic direction following the leadership transition.

Meanwhile, Kress said Nvidia was raising its fiscal 2028 outlook and expected revenue growth of approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% previously and on a higher fiscal 2027 base.

data.title: Nvidia earnings: investors still need answers to two key questions
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) more than doubled its quarterly revenue to nearly $116 billion in its fiscal Q3 and issued impressive guidance for the future as well.

But buying NVDA shares this morning means betting on growth that still has to be earned. Two questions matter for that bet:

  1. Can Nvidia keep delivering new chips on schedule and winning big orders without Jensen Huang?
  2. If tighter US rules choke off Chinese demand served through Singapore, can it turn those same chips into just as much profit somewhere else?

Nvidia stock is currently down nearly 35% versus its year-to-date high.

Key man risk remains alive for Nvidia stock

While the media narrative this morning is how Nvidia earnings essentially silence the “key man” risk, it’s worth noting that the company’s quarter ended Oct. 25 – about two weeks before its board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation.

Simply put, Huang ran Nvidia for the entire quarter.

So, the earnings beat, and even the guidance, tells investors that orders Nvidia had already secured translated into strong sales. The real test for interim CEO Colette Kress and NVDA stock actually begins with the “next round of orders.”

Kress told CNBC that key cloud customers were still asking for more computing power.

The harder question is whether those customers will keep committing billions to Nvidia’s next generation of chips.

A delayed launch or a large order that goes elsewhere could dent future earnings, turning investors less willing to pay a premium for each dollar Nvidia earns.

China remains a key overhang on NVDA shares

A chip can sit in a Singapore data centre and still do work for a customer in China – the new US rules target some of that remote access.

Nvidia recorded $11.05 billion, about 9.5% of quarterly sales, from direct customers headquartered in China and Hong Kong.

Its print leaves the amount of Chinese demand served through Singapore unknown.

On CNBC, Jim Cramer asked whether other buyers could absorb chips Nvidia might stop shipping to the region without pushing prices down.

Kress explained how Nvidia checks who will use the chips and whether data centres are ready.

But she gave no indication of how quickly alternative buyers could take delivery or whether they would pay the same price.

That remains a key overhang on Nvidia shares.

Technical setup warrants caution on Nvidia

Even from a technical perspective, NVDA shares have not turned attractive yet.

The AI darling currently sits firmly below major moving averages (MAs), with an RSI in the early 20s indicating intense selling pressure.

That said, Wall Street hasn’t thrown in the towel on Nvidia yet.

The consensus rating on the chip-maker remains at Strong Buy, with the mean price target of about $258 indicating massive upside potential from current levels.

data.title: When could Anthropic stock join the MSCI, Russell, FTSE and Nasdaq-100?
data.description:
Index funds may be among the larger buyers of Anthropic stock after it lists, but they will not all arrive on the first day, and they will not all arrive at once.

Anthropic is due to price its IPO on 18 November and to start trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on 19 November under the ticker ANT, as set out in Nasdaq Data Technical News #2026-28 and the company's latest S-1 amendment. The official range is still $70–$78 a share for 825 million Class A shares.

The timetable is now clearer than it was at the start of the roadshow, and slower than some early commentary suggested. Thanksgiving has pushed two FTSE Russell additions later into December. The S&P 500 is not in prospect at listing at all.

When could Anthropic join MSCI?

MSCI has published the rule, not the decision. In a 12 November announcement for its Global Standard indexes, it said it would apply its usual methodology for large IPOs.

To qualify for early inclusion, the stock must meet MSCI's eligibility rules, with the exception of the usual length-of-trading and liquidity screens, and must have a company full market capitalisation of at least 1.8 times the Interim Market Size-Segment Cutoff, plus a free-float-adjusted market capitalisation of at least 1.8 times one-half of that cutoff, measured at the close of the first or second trading day.

Any greenshoe publicly announced as exercised before MSCI's decision would be included in those calculations.

The decision would be announced no earlier than the first day of trading and no later than before the opening of the third trading day. If the first trade is on 19 November, that third session would be Monday, 23 November. Early inclusions are usually effective as of the close of the tenth trading day, but if that date falls close to a scheduled review, the addition is aligned with the review instead.

On that basis, if ANT begins trading on 19 November and meets the tests, inclusion would be effective as of the close on 30 November 2026, or 1 December, coinciding with the November 2026 Index Review. That remains a conditional outcome.

Why did FTSE Russell push the dates back?

Because a standard fast-entry calendar would have landed next to Thanksgiving.

In two informative notices dated 13 November, FTSE Russell said it will confirm after the first day of trading whether Anthropic meets the tests, and will issue a further notice after that session if it does.

For the Russell US Equity Indexes, the fast-entry threshold is $17.942 billion of investable market capitalisation. The usual rule would add an eligible IPO after the close of the fifth trading day. If the first trade is on 19 or 20 November, FTSE Russell said the stock would instead be added with the December semi-annual reconstitution, after the close on Friday, 11 December, effective at the open on Monday, 14 December, if it meets the criteria.

For the FTSE Global Equity Index Series, the current fast-entry thresholds for FTSE North America are $43.741 billion of full market capitalisation and $14.580 billion of investable market capitalisation. If ANT qualifies, it would be added with the December review, after the close on Friday, 18 December, effective at the open on Monday, 21 December. Until those notices appear, inclusion is not confirmed.

Could ANT enter the Nasdaq-100 in December?

It might be considered. It has not been added. Nasdaq has not published a notice naming ANT as a Nasdaq-100 constituent.

Under the Nasdaq-100 methodology, a newly listed security can be considered for fast-track inclusion if it meets the index's eligibility and ranking tests.

The next scheduled reconstitution is widely expected to take effect on 21 December 2026, and some secondary reports have already treated that date as a likely entry point for Anthropic. That is a reading of the rulebook, not an official Nasdaq announcement, and should not be confused with the MSCI and FTSE Russell calendars above.

Why is the S&P 500 not in play at listing?

Because it still requires a seasoning period and a profitability test, and S&P Dow Jones Indices has declined to waive either for megacap companies.

In the results of a June 2026 consultation, S&P DJI left the S&P 500 rules unchanged: IPOs should have traded on an eligible exchange for at least 12 months, and companies must have positive GAAP net income from continuing operations in the most recent quarter and in the sum of the most recent four consecutive quarters.

If ANT lists on 19 November 2026, the 12-month clock would run into mid-November 2027. The profitability test is a separate hurdle.

Anthropic's prospectus shows a history of GAAP net losses, including a net loss of $104.0 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, of which $94.3 billion was fair-value changes on convertible notes and related instruments.

Even if much of that loss is non-cash, it is still a GAAP net loss, so the stock would not meet the earnings screen at listing.

The broader S&P Total Market Index has a separate fast-track process for eligible IPOs, which Reuters noted on 12 November. That is not an S&P 500 inclusion.

How much passive demand is expected?

The useful estimate on the table is already a few days old, and the calendar has since moved.

Index-rebalance firm Intropic estimated that passive demand from index-tracking funds would account for about 28% of the shares on offer, or roughly $19 billion.

FTSE Russell's Thanksgiving deferral means part of that buying, if it materialises, now sits in mid-December for the Russell US indexes and in the third week of December for FTSE GEIS. MSCI's potential 1 December effective date is still relatively early.

The $19 billion figure should be read as an estimate prepared against a faster calendar, not as a confirmed order for the first two weeks of trading.

Index funds that do buy will be doing so because the rules require it, which can still matter in early trading, but it does not guarantee a higher price.

Investors who want exposure through an index fund will need to check whether the tracker they hold follows a benchmark that is actually adding the stock, and on which date.

Buying ANT directly once trading begins is a different route.

data.title: DJT stock is at a record low: Why Trump Media could fall to $2 or lower
data.description:
Trump Media stock has remained under pressure this week and is hovering near its all-time low. DJT traded at $4 on Wednesday, down more than 70% so far this year. The sell-off may continue through the rest of the year, and there is a risk that the stock could fall below $2 over the longer term.

Trump Media faces a $1 billion debt wall

Trump Media, the parent company of Truth Social, is facing some major risks. One of them is that the company needs to repay about $1 billion by November 30. 

The debt emerged from the company’s decision to invest in Bitcoin, mirroring the strategy that Michael Saylor perfected at Strategy. 

It issued that debt in May last year. According to its prospectus, the debt matures on May 29 2028, but its holders can demand cash repayment on November 30th. The stock remains much lower than its conversion price, meaning that cash repayment is more attractive than converting. 

The company is now in a bind as it does not have that money in its balance sheet. As a result, the options include selling its Bitcoin holdings, which are now valued at about $1 billion. It can also decide to raise cash by selling shares, a move that will dilute its shareholders. Also, it can use some of its cash to repay the debt.

These challenges are compounded by the ongoing deterioration of Bitcoin and other coins. Bitcoin dropped to $63,857, down by 27% from its highest point in October. It has also dropped by nearly 50% from its highest point in October last year. At its all-time high, its Bitcoin holdings were worth about $2 billion. 

Trump Media is facing other challenges

The company is facing other risks. For example, Democrats recently won the Senate and the House of Representatives, and will most likely investigate the company for its Truth+ product. This is a service that lets people and companies pay about $100,000 a month to get access to Truth posts from the most active users on its platform. This service is widely seen as a way for Trump to monetize the presidency. 

Further, Trump’s approval rating has continued falling after the midterm elections. This rating stands at 31%, the lowest point of both of his terms, and the trend may continue since he is not working to end the Iran war. As a result, with the president’s popularity fading, there is a likelihood that traffic to the website will also drop. Indeed, SimilarWeb data shows that the traffic dropped by over 22% in October.

Trump Media has a narrow path for making real profits. Its last earnings report showed that its net profit rose to over $409 million from a loss of $238 million in the previous quarter. However, most of these profits came from its Bitcoin gains, which have now reversed.

Further, in the long term, it is hard to imagine how the company survives, especially when Trump leaves office.

DJT stock price technical analysis

Trump Media stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the DJT stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months and is now at its all-time low. It has already dropped below the important support level of $6.96, its lowest level on June 25. 

The stock remains below all moving averages and the Ichimoku cloud, a sign that bears remain in control. Also, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and the MACD have continued moving downwards. 

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling as its fundamentals deteriorate. In the long term, this decline may hit $2 and below.
